verdict: RUNG (t0 is F154's p1 on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct): 2 cells, worst error 0.00e+00. Identical. ANTI-VACUITY: 0 model(s) lack room to move both ways, so both can show either direction. PRIMARY, is either INSTRUCT model raised by any of the twelve texts? Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct raw 0.573: 0 up of 12 (none); gemma-2-2b-it raw 0.714: 1 up of 12 (t2). Total 1 of 24. RAISED. F151's 18-of-18 was a text-sampling artefact on the instruct cohort too, just as F152 showed for base models. There is NO instruct-vs-base cohort difference here, and the programme's 'no clean factors -- only text x weights pairs' pattern goes FOUR for four. SECONDARY, structural vs prose on the SAME twelve texts F155 used on base models: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct struct 0/6, prose 0/6; gemma-2-2b-it struct 1/6, prose 0/6. F155's base-model comparison: Falcon3-1B 4/6 vs 1/6, Minerva 3/6 vs 1/6, Qwen1.5 0/6 vs 1/6, SmolLM 1/6 vs 0/6. BOUNDARY: TWO instruct models, twelve texts, ONE length (9 tokens), one corpus. A null here is 'these two resisted these twelve', NOT 'instruct models are unraisable' -- and this programme's history is that the distinction is where claims die. `gemma-2-2b-it` is also the only FRAGMENTED model in the domain work, so cohort and class are confounded in it.
